title: Production Vision 2025
body: When the ten points get treated as a poster on the wall instead of a daily checklist, the gaps show up exactly where ADW keeps bleeding tons — waste stripping falls behind while ore holds steady, because ore is what gets chased when time runs short. Chasing ore now borrows against bench access later.
keyPoints: Volume/hour beats volume/day. A fleet that grinds for six hours and sits for six is not the same as one that runs steady for twelve — available hours are the denominator, so closing availability-utilization gaps is the actual job, not a side metric.
Excavator positioning sets the pace for the whole fleet. Too far off the face, wrong angle, poor berm clearance — that's where backloading and idle truck time start, not at the truck.
Bench height has to be right, not just safe. Too low and you're loading in five passes instead of two; too high and you've created a hazard. Both cost production.
Mine sequentially. Stripping layers progressively keeps face height consistent and lets grade control do its job — cherry-picking faces creates the congestion that makes everything downstream harder.
Safety and productivity aren't opposites here — a plan that hits target by cutting corners on Life Saving Rules isn't actually running to vision, it's borrowing against the next incident.
apply: Check whether waste is genuinely getting stripped ahead of the ore blocks you're feeding, or whether the crews are quietly prioritizing ore faces because they're easier — that trade looks fine on today's tonnage report and shows up as a bench-access problem in a few weeks.
